summary: Gives reasons for a reasonably large default MTU for IP over ATM AAL5 and presents the default value to use. It was a standards-track proposal. It was replaced by RFC 2225.

eli5.summary: Bigger boxes mean fewer trips. This says how big the standard packet size should be on ATM links. A newer document replaced it.

questions: what is the default ip mtu for atm aal5
how big should packets be on atm networks
subtitle: Set the default packet size for IP over ATM AAL5 to 9180 octets

tldr.problem: Applications like NFS use large frame sizes (8 KB or more), and IP fragmentation reduces performance. A sensible default MTU for IP over ATM AAL5 was needed, matching the MTU used for IP over SMDS.
tldr.mechanism: The default IP MTU for ATM AAL5 is set to 9180 octets, the same size used for IP over SMDS, to support large application frames and reduce fragmentation.
tldr.outcome: Networks have a clear default MTU value, enabling better interoperability and reducing IP fragmentation. Implementations must support this default and implement Path MTU Discovery.

today: RFC 1626 is a Proposed Standard for the default MTU for IP over ATM AAL5. It was replaced by RFC 2225.

sections.title: Why a Large Default MTU
sections.content:
Protocols like NFS default to 8192-byte frames. When IP adds its header along with UDP and other headers (about 28 bytes), NFS would prefer an MTU of at least 8300 octets. Larger packet sizes reduce fragmentation and improve performance, particularly for applications that send large frames.

Routers also perform better with larger packets because most router costs relate to the number of packets handled rather than bytes transferred.
sections.eli5: Big applications send big packages. Splitting them up wastes time, so the network should handle big packages by default.

sections.title: The Default Value
sections.content:
The default IP MTU for IP over ATM AAL5 is set to 9180 octets. This matches the MTU used for IP over SMDS (RFC 1209), ensuring consistency across similar technologies and reducing fragmentation across different subnet types.

All implementations compliant with this specification must support at least this default MTU value.
sections.eli5: Use 9180 bytes as the standard size. It is the same size as another network technology uses.

sections.title: Negotiating the MTU
sections.content:
For Permanent Virtual Circuits (PVCs), both parties use the default unless they have agreed in advance on a different value. For Switched Virtual Circuits (SVCs), implementations MUST negotiate the AAL CPCS-SDU size using ATM signalling protocol. The ATM signalling protocol allows separate MTU values in each direction (forward and backward). If the called endpoint wishes a smaller MTU, it sets the desired value in the CONNECT message responding to the SETUP. If either endpoint receives CPCS-SDUs in excess of the negotiated MTU size, it may use IP fragmentation or may clear the call.

Path MTU Discovery (RFC 1191) is required for all router implementations and recommended for hosts, since ATM MTU sizes differ significantly from older technologies like Ethernet and FDDI.
sections.eli5: Phone-like connections use a fixed size. Dial-up connections can agree on a size first. All systems should be ready if a packet needs to be split.

sections.title: Status
sections.content: RFC 1626 is a Proposed Standard from 1994. The default MTU value of 9180 octets remains in use, though later specifications such as RFC 2225 refined and replaced this document with updated guidance on IP over ATM.
sections.eli5: This standard was later updated by a newer specification, but the 9180 size is still used today.
